How your sober time is calculated

The day count is the number of calendar days between your start date and today. Your start date is day zero. The breakdown counts years, months, and days, accounting for different month lengths. Dates use your device’s local time zone; daylight-saving changes do not change the day count.

Your next milestone may be a set number of days or a calendar anniversary. A month is not always 30 days. You can enter any personal start date; the calculator does not choose a sobriety date for you.

Committed for iPhone and Apple Watch

Keep your progress somewhere you’ll see it.

Committed tracks the time since a date, your milestones, and more than one commitment. It works on iPhone and Apple Watch, including widgets and complications.

You can use it without creating an account. The app does not contain ads, analytics, or a social feed. Tracking is free with no time limit. The optional Lifetime Unlock adds premium features with a one-time purchase. See your local App Store for pricing.

Common questions

Before you download.

What can I track?
Sobriety, nicotine, social media, or another personal commitment.
Do I need an account?
No. Your information stays on your devices and can sync through your private iCloud account if you enable backup.
Is it a subscription?
No. Committed is free to use, with no time limit. Lifetime Unlock is an optional one-time purchase for premium features. See your local App Store for pricing.
Does it work on Apple Watch?
Yes. Lifetime Unlock includes an Apple Watch app and complications for supported watch faces.
